# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [yellow]
STRIP painted [blue] [red] [red]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[6] 2:[8] 3:[7] 4:[0] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[white]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

I need to communicate what I see to Mute (via speech or gesture) and to Blind (via speech). Mute already gestured a single ☝ to me - possibly asking about display, or just an opener. Since Mute cannot hear, I can only reach them via gesture. Blind can only be reached via my speech.

Let me report the full bomb state clearly to Blind (who needs to act) and to Mute (who has the manual and needs facts to match against instructions). Since I can speak to both at once, I'll do that - Mute receives speech too? Wait - checking channels: "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it." Yes, speech reaches both. Only gesture is separate, and Mute cannot speak back, only gesture to me.

So I should speak the full details to both, unnamed, so both get it.

```
speak(text="Display shows 7. Light is yellow. Strip painted blue red red, in that order. Keypad engraved 1 is 6, 2 is 8, 3 is 7, 4 is 0, it accepts 1 digit, nothing entered yet. Wires in order 1 blue 2 yellow 3 orange 4 red 5 purple 6 white.")
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫱 ✋]

Mute gestured two symbols this time: 🫱 ✋. Since Mute can't speak, they're trying to signal something to me using gestures — but a gesture only means something once we've agreed on meaning, and we haven't established any code. I can't interpret this yet. I should acknowledge that the display and light changed (display 7→6, light yellow→red), which seems important — possibly the keypad digit relates to display, and light color might be reacting to something Blind is doing to wires already.

I should keep feeding full state to both, and note the changes explicitly so Blind/Mute can correlate their actions with what changed.

```
speak(text="Update: display changed to 6. Light changed to red. Strip still blue red red. Keypad still shows 1 is 6, 2 is 8, 3 is 7, 4 is 0, accepts 1 digit, nothing entered. Wires unchanged: 1 blue 2 yellow 3 orange 4 red 5 purple 6 white.")
wait()
```

WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[white]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 🫳]

The light seems to be cycling (yellow, red, blue...) and display toggling between 7 and 6. This looks like it might be a timer or a state that Blind is cycling through by testing something (maybe a button or dial), waiting for a specific combination that matches the manual. Mute's gestures are likely reactions to what Blind is doing, relayed to me, but I can't decode them without a shared code — and I have no way to ask Mute questions since Mute can't hear speech either... wait, actually Mute *can* hear? Let's check: Mute "Cannot speak, or touch the bomb" — nothing about hearing. Mute isn't listed as deaf. So Mute can hear speech from others (Blind and Deaf can speak, and Mute would receive it since only Deaf cannot hear).

So I can actually ask Mute things via speech, and Mute can respond only via gesture back to me. Let me try asking clarifying questions.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I see display alternating between 7 and 6, light cycling yellow red blue, strip blue red red, keypad shows 6 8 7 0 needs 1 digit. Wires blue yellow orange red purple white in order 1 to 6. Gesture thumbs up if the manual matches strip colors, thumbs down if it matches wire colors.")
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🙏 🖐]

Interesting — Blind just gestured to me too, meaning Blind can see gestures? Wait, no — Blind cannot see anything ("Cannot see a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed"). Let me re-check: the rules say "gesture(to=...)" — but if Blind can't see, how would Blind gesture to me and how would I "receive" it as gesture content?

Actually wait, re-reading: gestures are made with hands. Blind can still *make* gestures (hands work), just can't *see* them. The channel rule states "Whoever can see receives it" — I can see, so I receive Blind's gesture normally. Blind is producing gestures but doing so "blind" - probably reactionary, not visually informed. This is just how the game engine reports it; I'll treat it as data I received.

Blind's gesture: 🙏 🖐 — no established meaning. Given Blind cannot see gestures, this is odd but I'll take it as attempted signal, though I have no way to interpret it and Blind won't get an answer back from gestures since Blind can't see. I can only speak to Blind.

So none of display/light/keypad numbers match. Only wire colors matter per Mute. Let me ask about the strip order or count — maybe manual says "cut wire matching color that appears twice in strip" (red appears twice). Or maybe order matters: cut wire in position matching count of a color.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Does the manual say to cut the wire whose color matches a color that repeats, thumbs up yes thumbs down no?")
speak(to="blind", text="Standby, still decoding manual with mute. Do not act yet.")
wait()
```
